title: Launch and diagnostic: critical features of a movement and what each contributes
focus: critical features of a movement and what each contributes
standards: Michigan PE Standard 1: Demonstrates competency in a variety of motor skills and movement patterns. [Michigan PE Grades 9-12 LEVEL 1 (foundational high-school physical education)]
Michigan PE Standard 2: Applies knowledge of concepts, principles, strategies and tactics related to movement. [Michigan PE Grades 9-12 LEVEL 1 (foundational high-school physical education)]

standards_mapping.standard: Michigan PE Standard 1: Demonstrates competency in a variety of motor skills and movement patterns.
standards_mapping.level: Michigan PE Grades 9-12 LEVEL 1 (foundational high-school physical education)
standards_mapping.note: Standard statement and the grades 9-12 LEVEL 1 / LEVEL 2 structure confirmed against the official MDE source; per-outcome codes were not legible from that source and none is claimed.

standards_mapping.framework: Michigan K-12 Physical Education Standards (State Board approved 2017)
standards_mapping.standard: Michigan PE Standard 2: Applies knowledge of concepts, principles, strategies and tactics related to movement.
standards_mapping.level: Michigan PE Grades 9-12 LEVEL 1 (foundational high-school physical education)

essential_question: How do I find the flaw in my own movement without anyone filming me?
learning_objectives: Perform, adapt, or describe critical features of a movement and what each contributes safely at an intensity, range, and pace the learner sets.
Explain the movement, tactical, or training principle behind critical features of a movement and what each contributes and why it works.
Self-assess critical features of a movement and what each contributes against stated criteria and name the next adjustment, without comparing to any other person.
success_criteria: The learner completes or fully describes the critical features of a movement and what each contributes task using a version their body and setting allow.
The learner gives a cue, principle, tactic, or documented process rather than an unexplained result.
The learner self-assesses against the stated criteria and identifies one next adjustment.
materials: equipment for the chosen skill or a substitute

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Run the space, surface, footwear, and equipment check, then a learner-led warm-up. Restate the stop rule before any work on critical features of a movement and what each contributes.

Teach the cues, principle, or tactic behind critical features of a movement and what each contributes. Demonstrate or describe it, name the critical features, and show at least one adapted version alongside the standard version — not after it.

Practise critical features of a movement and what each contributes with feedback on cues and decisions only. Feedback addresses the movement or the choice, never the learner's body, size, or appearance. Fade prompting as control improves.
Learner applies critical features of a movement and what each contributes in a new situation at a self-set intensity and records what they did, what they noticed, and what they would adjust.

Cool down, then in one concise response explain the key idea behind critical features of a movement and what each contributes and name one adjustment for next session. No recording or photograph is taken.

student_activity: Learner applies critical features of a movement and what each contributes in a new situation at a self-set intensity and records what they did, noticed, and would adjust.
formative_check: In one concise response, explain the key idea behind critical features of a movement and what each contributes and name one adjustment for the next session.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score safe participation, skill cues, tactical reasoning, self-management, and revision. Accept any version of the task the learner’s body and setting allow as full credit. Never score body size, weight, body composition, appearance, speed alone, or comparison with another person.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the simplest version of critical features of a movement and what each contributes — slower, smaller range, closer target, or seated — then rebuild.
Ask the learner to explain the cue or tactic behind critical features of a movement and what each contributes before adding intensity or complexity.
Confirm the specific cue that worked, offer one varied application of critical features of a movement and what each contributes, and avoid unnecessary remediation.
Name the observable movement pattern neutrally, contrast it with the critical features, and schedule varied practice.

adaptive_tutor_routes.signal: pain, dizziness, breathlessness, or head impact
adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Stop immediately, tell an adult, and do not resume in this session. This is never recorded as a failed attempt.
Offer the adapted, seated, solo, or described version of critical features of a movement and what each contributes; the alternate route is full credit and is not logged as a refusal.

Require accurate independent performance or description plus explanation on a later occasion or in a different setting before marking critical features of a movement and what each contributes mastered.

mastery_rule: Do not mark mastery from one session. Use safe participation, skill cues, tactical decisions, self-management, personal progress against the learner’s own stated task, and self-assessment — without body-size scoring; require accurate independent evidence and successful transfer or retrieval on at least two occasions separated by time or setting.
extension: Apply critical features of a movement and what each contributes under a new constraint, in a different activity, or teach the cue to someone else — without completing another learner's graded work.
accessibility_and_accommodations: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, demonstrated, or described responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, rest-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, or response mode.
Every movement task has a seated, supported, reduced-range, reduced-pace, and solo version that reaches the same standard.
Any skill the learner can perform, in any range or position, is a valid choice, including a mobility-aid skill or a seated skill. Analysis may be described, drawn, or tabled.
safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, non-shaming language about bodies, ability, and effort.
Allow a pause, rest, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Check space, footwear, surface, weather, and equipment before movement.
Stop for pain, dizziness, breathing difficulty, head impact, or unsafe conditions and tell an adult.
Score skill, strategy, self-management, consistency, and reflection — never body size, weight, weight change, body composition, appearance, or comparison with another person.
Do not require weight, BMI, body-fat, body measurement, fitness-test norms, percentile ranks, calorie counts, or diet goals at any point.
Do not require a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as evidence; described, written, and demonstrated-to-one-adult evidence is the intended route.
Do not require performance in front of an audience, a group, or spectators.
No video or photograph is required, requested, or used for analysis; self-observation and outcome evidence are the intended method, not a fallback.
inclusive_adaptation: Any skill the learner can perform, in any range or position, is a valid choice, including a mobility-aid skill or a seated skill. Analysis may be described, drawn, or tabled.

guardian_safety.equipment: Equipment for the chosen skill; substitutes are always acceptable.
guardian_safety.environment: Space appropriate to the chosen skill.
guardian_safety.movement_hazards: Repeated practice of one pattern. Learner applies the stop rule and varies practice to avoid overuse.
guardian_safety.supervision_note: Guardian approves the chosen skill and the practice space.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, described demonstration, or short clip supporting critical features of a movement and what each contributes.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, cue lists, alt text, a transcript, or an adult demonstration. No lesson requires media, and no learner media is ever produced.

parent_or_guardian_visibility: Share the lesson target, completion state, evidence type, and next instructional step. Do not expose body data, fitness scores, photographs, video, recordings, or comparisons with other learners. For safety-critical units, record only the guardian confirmation that was required.
home_connection: Invite the learner to notice or try one safe, optional example of critical features of a movement and what each contributes in daily life. No purchase, account creation, photograph, recording, or public performance is required.

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Run the space, surface, footwear, and equipment check, then a learner-led warm-up. Restate the stop rule before any work on creating and exploiting space across a net.

student_activity: Learner applies creating and exploiting space across a net in a new situation at a self-set intensity and records what they did, noticed, and would adjust.
formative_check: In one concise response, explain the key idea behind creating and exploiting space across a net and name one adjustment for the next session.

essential_question: How do I build a sequence that says something and still works as movement?
learning_objectives: Perform, adapt, or describe space, time, weight, and flow as movement qualities safely at an intensity, range, and pace the learner sets.
Explain the movement, tactical, or training principle behind space, time, weight, and flow as movement qualities and why it works.
Self-assess space, time, weight, and flow as movement qualities against stated criteria and name the next adjustment, without comparing to any other person.
success_criteria: The learner completes or fully describes the space, time, weight, and flow as movement qualities task using a version their body and setting allow.
The learner gives a cue, principle, tactic, or documented process rather than an unexplained result.
The learner self-assesses against the stated criteria and identifies one next adjustment.

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Run the space, surface, footwear, and equipment check, then a learner-led warm-up. Restate the stop rule before any work on space, time, weight, and flow as movement qualities.

Teach the cues, principle, or tactic behind space, time, weight, and flow as movement qualities. Demonstrate or describe it, name the critical features, and show at least one adapted version alongside the standard version — not after it.

Practise space, time, weight, and flow as movement qualities with feedback on cues and decisions only. Feedback addresses the movement or the choice, never the learner's body, size, or appearance. Fade prompting as control improves.
Learner applies space, time, weight, and flow as movement qualities in a new situation at a self-set intensity and records what they did, what they noticed, and what they would adjust.
Cool down, then in one concise response explain the key idea behind space, time, weight, and flow as movement qualities and name one adjustment for next session. No recording or photograph is taken.

student_activity: Learner applies space, time, weight, and flow as movement qualities in a new situation at a self-set intensity and records what they did, noticed, and would adjust.
formative_check: In one concise response, explain the key idea behind space, time, weight, and flow as movement qualities and name one adjustment for the next session.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score safe participation, skill cues, tactical reasoning, self-management, and revision. Accept any version of the task the learner’s body and setting allow as full credit. Never score body size, weight, body composition, appearance, speed alone, or comparison with another person.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the simplest version of space, time, weight, and flow as movement qualities — slower, smaller range, closer target, or seated — then rebuild.
Ask the learner to explain the cue or tactic behind space, time, weight, and flow as movement qualities before adding intensity or complexity.
Confirm the specific cue that worked, offer one varied application of space, time, weight, and flow as movement qualities, and avoid unnecessary remediation.
Name the observable movement pattern neutrally, contrast it with the critical features, and schedule varied practice.

adaptive_tutor_routes.signal: pain, dizziness, breathlessness, or head impact
adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Stop immediately, tell an adult, and do not resume in this session. This is never recorded as a failed attempt.
Offer the adapted, seated, solo, or described version of space, time, weight, and flow as movement qualities; the alternate route is full credit and is not logged as a refusal.
Require accurate independent performance or description plus explanation on a later occasion or in a different setting before marking space, time, weight, and flow as movement qualities mastered.

mastery_rule: Do not mark mastery from one session. Use safe participation, skill cues, tactical decisions, self-management, personal progress against the learner’s own stated task, and self-assessment — without body-size scoring; require accurate independent evidence and successful transfer or retrieval on at least two occasions separated by time or setting.
extension: Apply space, time, weight, and flow as movement qualities under a new constraint, in a different activity, or teach the cue to someone else — without completing another learner's graded work.
accessibility_and_accommodations: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, demonstrated, or described responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, rest-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, or response mode.
Every movement task has a seated, supported, reduced-range, reduced-pace, and solo version that reaches the same standard.
Sequences may be seated, small-range, hand-and-arm only, or built at any tempo. Notation, storyboard, or written description is a full alternative to performing.
safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, non-shaming language about bodies, ability, and effort.
Allow a pause, rest, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Check space, footwear, surface, weather, and equipment before movement.
Stop for pain, dizziness, breathing difficulty, head impact, or unsafe conditions and tell an adult.
Score skill, strategy, self-management, consistency, and reflection — never body size, weight, weight change, body composition, appearance, or comparison with another person.
Do not require weight, BMI, body-fat, body measurement, fitness-test norms, percentile ranks, calorie counts, or diet goals at any point.
Do not require a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as evidence; described, written, and demonstrated-to-one-adult evidence is the intended route.
Do not require performance in front of an audience, a group, or spectators.
No performance is filmed, photographed, recorded, or shown beyond one trusted adult, and the learner may decline to perform without losing credit.
inclusive_adaptation: Sequences may be seated, small-range, hand-and-arm only, or built at any tempo. Notation, storyboard, or written description is a full alternative to performing.

guardian_safety.equipment: Music source only.
guardian_safety.environment: Clear space with safe flooring.
guardian_safety.movement_hazards: Turning, level changes, travel; learner sets range and tempo.
guardian_safety.supervision_note: Guardian confirms who, if anyone, watches; the default is no audience.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, described demonstration, or short clip supporting space, time, weight, and flow as movement qualities.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, cue lists, alt text, a transcript, or an adult demonstration. No lesson requires media, and no learner media is ever produced.

parent_or_guardian_visibility: Share the lesson target, completion state, evidence type, and next instructional step. Do not expose body data, fitness scores, photographs, video, recordings, or comparisons with other learners. For safety-critical units, record only the guardian confirmation that was required.
home_connection: Invite the learner to notice or try one safe, optional example of space, time, weight, and flow as movement qualities in daily life. No purchase, account creation, photograph, recording, or public performance is required.

essential_question: What have I built that is worth specializing in?
learning_objectives: Perform, adapt, or describe identifying the strongest and weakest of the five for the learner safely at an intensity, range, and pace the learner sets.
Explain the movement, tactical, or training principle behind identifying the strongest and weakest of the five for the learner and why it works.
Self-assess identifying the strongest and weakest of the five for the learner against stated criteria and name the next adjustment, without comparing to any other person.
success_criteria: The learner completes or fully describes the identifying the strongest and weakest of the five for the learner task using a version their body and setting allow.
The learner gives a cue, principle, tactic, or documented process rather than an unexplained result.
The learner self-assesses against the stated criteria and identifies one next adjustment.

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Run the space, surface, footwear, and equipment check, then a learner-led warm-up. Restate the stop rule before any work on identifying the strongest and weakest of the five for the learner.

Teach the cues, principle, or tactic behind identifying the strongest and weakest of the five for the learner. Demonstrate or describe it, name the critical features, and show at least one adapted version alongside the standard version — not after it.

Practise identifying the strongest and weakest of the five for the learner with feedback on cues and decisions only. Feedback addresses the movement or the choice, never the learner's body, size, or appearance. Fade prompting as control improves.
Learner applies identifying the strongest and weakest of the five for the learner in a new situation at a self-set intensity and records what they did, what they noticed, and what they would adjust.

Cool down, then in one concise response explain the key idea behind identifying the strongest and weakest of the five for the learner and name one adjustment for next session. No recording or photograph is taken.

student_activity: Learner applies identifying the strongest and weakest of the five for the learner in a new situation at a self-set intensity and records what they did, noticed, and would adjust.
formative_check: In one concise response, explain the key idea behind identifying the strongest and weakest of the five for the learner and name one adjustment for the next session.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score safe participation, skill cues, tactical reasoning, self-management, and revision. Accept any version of the task the learner’s body and setting allow as full credit. Never score body size, weight, body composition, appearance, speed alone, or comparison with another person.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the simplest version of identifying the strongest and weakest of the five for the learner — slower, smaller range, closer target, or seated — then rebuild.
Ask the learner to explain the cue or tactic behind identifying the strongest and weakest of the five for the learner before adding intensity or complexity.
Confirm the specific cue that worked, offer one varied application of identifying the strongest and weakest of the five for the learner, and avoid unnecessary remediation.
Name the observable movement pattern neutrally, contrast it with the critical features, and schedule varied practice.

adaptive_tutor_routes.signal: pain, dizziness, breathlessness, or head impact
adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Stop immediately, tell an adult, and do not resume in this session. This is never recorded as a failed attempt.
Offer the adapted, seated, solo, or described version of identifying the strongest and weakest of the five for the learner; the alternate route is full credit and is not logged as a refusal.

Require accurate independent performance or description plus explanation on a later occasion or in a different setting before marking identifying the strongest and weakest of the five for the learner mastered.

mastery_rule: Do not mark mastery from one session. Use safe participation, skill cues, tactical decisions, self-management, personal progress against the learner’s own stated task, and self-assessment — without body-size scoring; require accurate independent evidence and successful transfer or retrieval on at least two occasions separated by time or setting.
extension: Apply identifying the strongest and weakest of the five for the learner under a new constraint, in a different activity, or teach the cue to someone else — without completing another learner's graded work.
accessibility_and_accommodations: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, demonstrated, or described responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, rest-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, or response mode.
Every movement task has a seated, supported, reduced-range, reduced-pace, and solo version that reaches the same standard.
Presentation may be spoken one-to-one, written, or submitted as an annotated document. No recording, photograph, or audience beyond one adult is required.
safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, non-shaming language about bodies, ability, and effort.
Allow a pause, rest, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Check space, footwear, surface, weather, and equipment before movement.
Stop for pain, dizziness, breathing difficulty, head impact, or unsafe conditions and tell an adult.
Score skill, strategy, self-management, consistency, and reflection — never body size, weight, weight change, body composition, appearance, or comparison with another person.
Do not require weight, BMI, body-fat, body measurement, fitness-test norms, percentile ranks, calorie counts, or diet goals at any point.
Do not require a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as evidence; described, written, and demonstrated-to-one-adult evidence is the intended route.
Do not require performance in front of an audience, a group, or spectators.
Evidence is described in words; no photographic or video proof of performance is requested or accepted as a requirement.
inclusive_adaptation: Presentation may be spoken one-to-one, written, or submitted as an annotated document. No recording, photograph, or audience beyond one adult is required.

guardian_safety.equipment: None.
guardian_safety.environment: Indoor space for a one-to-one review.
guardian_safety.movement_hazards: None expected.
guardian_safety.supervision_note: Guardian acts as reviewer. The review is a conversation, not a recorded artifact.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, described demonstration, or short clip supporting identifying the strongest and weakest of the five for the learner.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, cue lists, alt text, a transcript, or an adult demonstration. No lesson requires media, and no learner media is ever produced.

parent_or_guardian_visibility: Share the lesson target, completion state, evidence type, and next instructional step. Do not expose body data, fitness scores, photographs, video, recordings, or comparisons with other learners. For safety-critical units, record only the guardian confirmation that was required.
home_connection: Invite the learner to notice or try one safe, optional example of identifying the strongest and weakest of the five for the learner in daily life. No purchase, account creation, photograph, recording, or public performance is required.

essential_question: What have I built that is worth specializing in?
learning_objectives: Perform, adapt, or describe setting the safety and self-management rules that carry forward safely at an intensity, range, and pace the learner sets.
Explain the movement, tactical, or training principle behind setting the safety and self-management rules that carry forward and why it works.
Self-assess setting the safety and self-management rules that carry forward against stated criteria and name the next adjustment, without comparing to any other person.
success_criteria: The learner completes or fully describes the setting the safety and self-management rules that carry forward task using a version their body and setting allow.
The learner gives a cue, principle, tactic, or documented process rather than an unexplained result.
The learner self-assesses against the stated criteria and identifies one next adjustment.

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Run the space, surface, footwear, and equipment check, then a learner-led warm-up. Restate the stop rule before any work on setting the safety and self-management rules that carry forward.

Teach the cues, principle, or tactic behind setting the safety and self-management rules that carry forward. Demonstrate or describe it, name the critical features, and show at least one adapted version alongside the standard version — not after it.

Practise setting the safety and self-management rules that carry forward with feedback on cues and decisions only. Feedback addresses the movement or the choice, never the learner's body, size, or appearance. Fade prompting as control improves.
Learner applies setting the safety and self-management rules that carry forward in a new situation at a self-set intensity and records what they did, what they noticed, and what they would adjust.

Cool down, then in one concise response explain the key idea behind setting the safety and self-management rules that carry forward and name one adjustment for next session. No recording or photograph is taken.

student_activity: Learner applies setting the safety and self-management rules that carry forward in a new situation at a self-set intensity and records what they did, noticed, and would adjust.
formative_check: In one concise response, explain the key idea behind setting the safety and self-management rules that carry forward and name one adjustment for the next session.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score safe participation, skill cues, tactical reasoning, self-management, and revision. Accept any version of the task the learner’s body and setting allow as full credit. Never score body size, weight, body composition, appearance, speed alone, or comparison with another person.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the simplest version of setting the safety and self-management rules that carry forward — slower, smaller range, closer target, or seated — then rebuild.
Ask the learner to explain the cue or tactic behind setting the safety and self-management rules that carry forward before adding intensity or complexity.
Confirm the specific cue that worked, offer one varied application of setting the safety and self-management rules that carry forward, and avoid unnecessary remediation.
Name the observable movement pattern neutrally, contrast it with the critical features, and schedule varied practice.

adaptive_tutor_routes.signal: pain, dizziness, breathlessness, or head impact
adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Stop immediately, tell an adult, and do not resume in this session. This is never recorded as a failed attempt.
Offer the adapted, seated, solo, or described version of setting the safety and self-management rules that carry forward; the alternate route is full credit and is not logged as a refusal.

Require accurate independent performance or description plus explanation on a later occasion or in a different setting before marking setting the safety and self-management rules that carry forward mastered.

mastery_rule: Do not mark mastery from one session. Use safe participation, skill cues, tactical decisions, self-management, personal progress against the learner’s own stated task, and self-assessment — without body-size scoring; require accurate independent evidence and successful transfer or retrieval on at least two occasions separated by time or setting.
extension: Apply setting the safety and self-management rules that carry forward under a new constraint, in a different activity, or teach the cue to someone else — without completing another learner's graded work.
accessibility_and_accommodations: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, demonstrated, or described responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, rest-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, or response mode.
Every movement task has a seated, supported, reduced-range, reduced-pace, and solo version that reaches the same standard.
Presentation may be spoken one-to-one, written, or submitted as an annotated document. No recording, photograph, or audience beyond one adult is required.
safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, non-shaming language about bodies, ability, and effort.
Allow a pause, rest, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Check space, footwear, surface, weather, and equipment before movement.
Stop for pain, dizziness, breathing difficulty, head impact, or unsafe conditions and tell an adult.
Score skill, strategy, self-management, consistency, and reflection — never body size, weight, weight change, body composition, appearance, or comparison with another person.
Do not require weight, BMI, body-fat, body measurement, fitness-test norms, percentile ranks, calorie counts, or diet goals at any point.
Do not require a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as evidence; described, written, and demonstrated-to-one-adult evidence is the intended route.
Do not require performance in front of an audience, a group, or spectators.
Evidence is described in words; no photographic or video proof of performance is requested or accepted as a requirement.
inclusive_adaptation: Presentation may be spoken one-to-one, written, or submitted as an annotated document. No recording, photograph, or audience beyond one adult is required.

guardian_safety.equipment: None.
guardian_safety.environment: Indoor space for a one-to-one review.
guardian_safety.movement_hazards: None expected.
guardian_safety.supervision_note: Guardian acts as reviewer. The review is a conversation, not a recorded artifact.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, described demonstration, or short clip supporting setting the safety and self-management rules that carry forward.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, cue lists, alt text, a transcript, or an adult demonstration. No lesson requires media, and no learner media is ever produced.

parent_or_guardian_visibility: Share the lesson target, completion state, evidence type, and next instructional step. Do not expose body data, fitness scores, photographs, video, recordings, or comparisons with other learners. For safety-critical units, record only the guardian confirmation that was required.
home_connection: Invite the learner to notice or try one safe, optional example of setting the safety and self-management rules that carry forward in daily life. No purchase, account creation, photograph, recording, or public performance is required.

essential_question: What have I built that is worth specializing in?
learning_objectives: Sustain identifying the strongest and weakest of the five for the learner consolidated into the LEVEL 1 portfolio and defended, including the standard the learner is weakest in, holding the critical features when conditions stop being ideal.
Explain what changed about identifying the strongest and weakest of the five for the learner under that demand, and which cue or principle held and which broke down first.
Judge the learner's own identifying the strongest and weakest of the five for the learner against the criteria a second time and account for the difference from the first pass.
success_criteria: The learner holds identifying the strongest and weakest of the five for the learner consolidated into the LEVEL 1 portfolio and defended, including the standard the learner is weakest in, in whatever version their body and setting allow.
The learner names what degraded first and why, rather than reporting only whether it worked.
The learner compares this occasion with the earlier one and says what actually changed.

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Run the space, surface, footwear, and equipment check, then a learner-led warm-up. Restate the stop rule, and name the added demand explicitly before starting: identifying the strongest and weakest of the five for the learner consolidated into the LEVEL 1 portfolio and defended, including the standard the learner is weakest in.

Have the learner restate the critical features of identifying the strongest and weakest of the five for the learner from the earlier pass before any demonstration. Then introduce the transfer condition and ask which feature they expect to lose first, and why. Keep the adapted version available on equal terms.

Work identifying the strongest and weakest of the five for the learner consolidated into the LEVEL 1 portfolio and defended, including the standard the learner is weakest in. Feedback stays on the cue or the decision, never on the learner's body, size, or appearance. Reduce the demand rather than the standard if control breaks down, and say that is the intended response, not a failure.

Learner works identifying the strongest and weakest of the five for the learner independently under the condition at a self-set intensity, then records what held, what degraded first, and how this occasion differed from the earlier one.

Cool down, then in one concise response account for the difference between the two occasions of identifying the strongest and weakest of the five for the learner and name the adjustment that carries forward. No recording or photograph is taken.

student_activity: Learner works identifying the strongest and weakest of the five for the learner consolidated into the LEVEL 1 portfolio and defended, including the standard the learner is weakest in at a self-set intensity, then records what held, what degraded first, and how this occasion differed from the earlier one.
formative_check: In one concise response, say which feature of identifying the strongest and weakest of the five for the learner degraded first under the added demand, why, and what you would change before the next attempt.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score safe participation, skill cues, tactical reasoning, self-management, and revision. Accept any version of the task the learner’s body and setting allow as full credit. Never score body size, weight, body composition, appearance, speed alone, or comparison with another person.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the simplest version of identifying the strongest and weakest of the five for the learner — slower, smaller range, closer target, or seated — then rebuild.
Ask the learner to explain the cue or tactic behind identifying the strongest and weakest of the five for the learner before adding intensity or complexity.
Confirm the specific cue that worked, offer one varied application of identifying the strongest and weakest of the five for the learner, and avoid unnecessary remediation.
Name the observable movement pattern neutrally, contrast it with the critical features, and schedule varied practice.

adaptive_tutor_routes.signal: pain, dizziness, breathlessness, or head impact
adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Stop immediately, tell an adult, and do not resume in this session. This is never recorded as a failed attempt.
Offer the adapted, seated, solo, or described version of identifying the strongest and weakest of the five for the learner; the alternate route is full credit and is not logged as a refusal.

adaptive_tutor_routes.signal: transfer condition is too much today
adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Drop back to the first-pass version of identifying the strongest and weakest of the five for the learner for this session and re-attempt the added demand on a later occasion. Reducing the demand is the correct response and is scored as full participation.

Require accurate independent performance or description plus explanation on a later occasion or in a different setting before marking identifying the strongest and weakest of the five for the learner mastered.

mastery_rule: Do not mark mastery from one session. Use safe participation, skill cues, tactical decisions, self-management, personal progress against the learner’s own stated task, and self-assessment — without body-size scoring; require accurate independent evidence and successful transfer or retrieval on at least two occasions separated by time or setting.
extension: Design the next progression of identifying the strongest and weakest of the five for the learner yourself, or coach the transfer condition to someone else so that they succeed with it — without completing another learner's graded work.
accessibility_and_accommodations: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, demonstrated, or described responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, rest-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, or response mode.
Every movement task has a seated, supported, reduced-range, reduced-pace, and solo version that reaches the same standard.
Presentation may be spoken one-to-one, written, or submitted as an annotated document. No recording, photograph, or audience beyond one adult is required.
safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, non-shaming language about bodies, ability, and effort.
Allow a pause, rest, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Check space, footwear, surface, weather, and equipment before movement.
Stop for pain, dizziness, breathing difficulty, head impact, or unsafe conditions and tell an adult.
Score skill, strategy, self-management, consistency, and reflection — never body size, weight, weight change, body composition, appearance, or comparison with another person.
Do not require weight, BMI, body-fat, body measurement, fitness-test norms, percentile ranks, calorie counts, or diet goals at any point.
Do not require a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as evidence; described, written, and demonstrated-to-one-adult evidence is the intended route.
Do not require performance in front of an audience, a group, or spectators.
Evidence is described in words; no photographic or video proof of performance is requested or accepted as a requirement.
inclusive_adaptation: Presentation may be spoken one-to-one, written, or submitted as an annotated document. No recording, photograph, or audience beyond one adult is required.

guardian_safety.equipment: None.
guardian_safety.environment: Indoor space for a one-to-one review.
guardian_safety.movement_hazards: None expected.
guardian_safety.supervision_note: Guardian acts as reviewer. The review is a conversation, not a recorded artifact.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, described demonstration, or short clip supporting identifying the strongest and weakest of the five for the learner.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, cue lists, alt text, a transcript, or an adult demonstration. No lesson requires media, and no learner media is ever produced.

parent_or_guardian_visibility: Share the lesson target, completion state, evidence type, and next instructional step. Do not expose body data, fitness scores, photographs, video, recordings, or comparisons with other learners. For safety-critical units, record only the guardian confirmation that was required.
home_connection: Invite the learner to notice where identifying the strongest and weakest of the five for the learner shows up outside the session under real conditions. No purchase, account creation, photograph, recording, or public performance is required.

essential_question: What have I built that is worth specializing in?
learning_objectives: Sustain setting the safety and self-management rules that carry forward consolidated into the LEVEL 1 portfolio and defended, including the standard the learner is weakest in, holding the critical features when conditions stop being ideal.
Explain what changed about setting the safety and self-management rules that carry forward under that demand, and which cue or principle held and which broke down first.
Judge the learner's own setting the safety and self-management rules that carry forward against the criteria a second time and account for the difference from the first pass.
success_criteria: The learner holds setting the safety and self-management rules that carry forward consolidated into the LEVEL 1 portfolio and defended, including the standard the learner is weakest in, in whatever version their body and setting allow.
The learner names what degraded first and why, rather than reporting only whether it worked.
The learner compares this occasion with the earlier one and says what actually changed.

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Run the space, surface, footwear, and equipment check, then a learner-led warm-up. Restate the stop rule, and name the added demand explicitly before starting: setting the safety and self-management rules that carry forward consolidated into the LEVEL 1 portfolio and defended, including the standard the learner is weakest in.

Have the learner restate the critical features of setting the safety and self-management rules that carry forward from the earlier pass before any demonstration. Then introduce the transfer condition and ask which feature they expect to lose first, and why. Keep the adapted version available on equal terms.

Work setting the safety and self-management rules that carry forward consolidated into the LEVEL 1 portfolio and defended, including the standard the learner is weakest in. Feedback stays on the cue or the decision, never on the learner's body, size, or appearance. Reduce the demand rather than the standard if control breaks down, and say that is the intended response, not a failure.

Learner works setting the safety and self-management rules that carry forward independently under the condition at a self-set intensity, then records what held, what degraded first, and how this occasion differed from the earlier one.

Cool down, then in one concise response account for the difference between the two occasions of setting the safety and self-management rules that carry forward and name the adjustment that carries forward. No recording or photograph is taken.

student_activity: Learner works setting the safety and self-management rules that carry forward consolidated into the LEVEL 1 portfolio and defended, including the standard the learner is weakest in at a self-set intensity, then records what held, what degraded first, and how this occasion differed from the earlier one.
formative_check: In one concise response, say which feature of setting the safety and self-management rules that carry forward degraded first under the added demand, why, and what you would change before the next attempt.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score safe participation, skill cues, tactical reasoning, self-management, and revision. Accept any version of the task the learner’s body and setting allow as full credit. Never score body size, weight, body composition, appearance, speed alone, or comparison with another person.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the simplest version of setting the safety and self-management rules that carry forward — slower, smaller range, closer target, or seated — then rebuild.
Ask the learner to explain the cue or tactic behind setting the safety and self-management rules that carry forward before adding intensity or complexity.
Confirm the specific cue that worked, offer one varied application of setting the safety and self-management rules that carry forward, and avoid unnecessary remediation.
Name the observable movement pattern neutrally, contrast it with the critical features, and schedule varied practice.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Stop immediately, tell an adult, and do not resume in this session. This is never recorded as a failed attempt.
Offer the adapted, seated, solo, or described version of setting the safety and self-management rules that carry forward; the alternate route is full credit and is not logged as a refusal.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Drop back to the first-pass version of setting the safety and self-management rules that carry forward for this session and re-attempt the added demand on a later occasion. Reducing the demand is the correct response and is scored as full participation.

Require accurate independent performance or description plus explanation on a later occasion or in a different setting before marking setting the safety and self-management rules that carry forward mastered.
